from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["We seek roots where a curve crosses zero.", "Start with a guess on the curve.", "Draw a tangent line at that point.", "Follow the tangent down to the axis.", "Repeat this to find the root."]
        self.setup_layout("The Quest for the Root (Prerequisites & Intuition)", lecture_lines)
        
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-2, 5], y_range=[-2, 5], axis_config={"include_tip": False})
        curve = axes.plot(lambda x: 0.5 * (x - 2)**2 - 1, color=WHITE)
        root_dot = Dot(axes.c2p(2, -1), color="#FF0000")
        
        pencil = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/pencil.svg")
        ruler = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/ruler.svg")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FF0000")
        self.play(Create(axes), Create(curve))
        self.play(FadeIn(root_dot))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FFFF")
        x0 = 4
        p0 = Dot(axes.c2p(x0, 0.5 * (x0 - 2)**2 - 1), color="#00FFFF")
        pencil_obj = self.place_at_grid(pencil, "B3", scale_factor=0.3)
        pencil_obj.next_to(p0, UP)
        self.play(FadeIn(p0), FadeIn(pencil_obj))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF00")
        # tangent line approximation
        tangent = Line(axes.c2p(3, -0.5), axes.c2p(5, 1.5), color="#FFFF00")
        ruler_obj = self.place_at_grid(ruler, "D4", scale_factor=0.3)
        self.play(Create(tangent), FadeIn(ruler_obj))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#00FF00")
        x1 = 2
        p1 = Dot(axes.c2p(x1, 0), color="#00FF00")
        self.play(MoveAlongPath(p1, tangent), run_time=2)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#FFA500")
        self.play(FadeOut(pencil_obj), FadeOut(ruler_obj))

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Use the Newton iteration formula.", "This creates a feedback loop.", "Each step gets closer to zero."]
        self.setup_layout("The Newton Iteration Formula", lecture_lines)
        
        # Formula
        formula = MathTex(r"x_{n+1} = x_n - \frac{f(x_n)}{f'(x_n)}", color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(formula, 'B2', scale_factor=1.2)
        
        # Asset: [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/loop.svg]
        loop_icon = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/loop.svg")
        self.place_at_grid(loop_icon, 'B4', scale_factor=0.5)
        
        # Dots for convergence
        dots = VGroup(*[Dot(color=YELLOW) for _ in range(4)])
        for i, dot in enumerate(dots):
            self.place_at_grid(dot, f'D{i+2}', scale_factor=1.0)
            dot.set_opacity(0)
            
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(formula))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(loop_icon))
        self.play(Rotate(loop_icon, angle=2*PI, run_time=2))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(GREEN)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        for dot in dots:
            self.play(FadeIn(dot), run_time=0.5)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Convergence can break unexpectedly.", "Guessing the root is chaotic.", "This forms a basin of attraction."]
        self.setup_layout("When Convergence Breaks: The Basin of Attraction", lecture_lines)
        
        # Assets
        compass = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/compass.svg")
        prism = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/prism.svg")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)
        graph = Axes(x_range=[-2, 2], y_range=[-2, 2], axis_config={"include_tip": False}).scale(0.5)
        curve = graph.plot(lambda x: x**3 - x)
        self.place_in_area(graph, 'A1', 'C3', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.place_in_area(curve, 'A1', 'C3', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(compass, 'A6', scale_factor=0.3)
        self.play(Create(graph), Create(curve), FadeIn(compass))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(GREEN)
        points = VGroup(*[Dot(point=graph.c2p(x, 0), color=YELLOW) for x in np.linspace(-1.5, 1.5, 10)])
        self.play(FadeIn(points))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(RED)
        basin_rect = Rectangle(width=2, height=2, fill_opacity=0.3, color=PURPLE)
        self.place_at_grid(basin_rect, 'D4')
        self.place_at_grid(prism, 'F6', scale_factor=0.4)
        self.play(Create(basin_rect), FadeIn(prism))
        self.wait(1)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Expand this into the complex plane.",
            "Colors reveal the roots for guesses.",
            "Boundaries show infinite, repeating patterns.",
            "Zoom reveals self-similar fractals.",
            "Beauty emerges from iterative chaos."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Birth of the Newton Fractal", lecture_lines)
        
        # Load asset
        grid_asset = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/grid.svg")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Expand this into the complex plane.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        grid1 = grid_asset.copy()
        self.place_in_area(grid1, "A1", "F6", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(grid1))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Colors reveal the roots for guesses.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(BLUE)
        colors = [RED, GREEN, BLUE]
        regions = VGroup(*[Square(side_length=1.5, fill_opacity=0.5, color=colors[i]).move_to(self.grid[f"C{2*i+1}"]) for i in range(3)])
        self.play(FadeIn(regions))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Boundaries show infinite, repeating patterns.
        self.lecture[2].set_color(PURPLE)
        boundary = VGroup(*[Dot(self.grid[f"D{i}"]).set_color(WHITE) for i in range(1, 7)])
        self.play(Flash(boundary))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Zoom reveals self-similar fractals.
        self.lecture[3].set_color(TEAL)
        self.play(grid1.animate.scale(2.0), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Beauty emerges from iterative chaos.
        self.lecture[4].set_color(GOLD)
        grid2 = grid_asset.copy()
        self.place_in_area(grid2, "A1", "F6", scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(FadeIn(grid2), Rotate(grid2, angle=PI/4))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary and Philosophical Takeaway", [
            "Deterministic rules generate extreme complexity.",
            "Fractals emerge from simple iteration.",
            "Beauty exists in infinite depth."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Fade in simple iteration equation in #FFFFFF.
        eq = MathTex(r"z_{n+1} = z_n - \frac{f(z_n)}{f'(z_n)}", color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(eq, 'B2', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(FadeIn(eq))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#88AAFF")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Morph equation into a complex fractal shape.
        # Representing a simplified fractal look as a complex geometric path
        fractal = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=0.1, color=BLUE).shift(i*RIGHT + j*UP) for i in range(-2, 3) for j in range(-2, 3)])
        self.place_at_grid(fractal, 'D3', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(eq, fractal))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#88FF88")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Slowly zoom into infinite depth, highlighting repeating patterns.
        self.play(fractal.animate.scale(3), run_time=3)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF8888")
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: From Roots to Chaos: Newton's Method and Fractals

sections.title: The Quest for the Root (Prerequisites & Intuition)
sections.content: Briefly introduce root-finding: we want to solve f(x)=0. Visualize this as finding where a curve crosses the X-axis. Explain the intuition of Newton's method: 'If you don't know the root, start with a guess, draw a tangent line to the curve at that point, and move to where that tangent hits the X-axis.'
sections.example: A hiker (the point) trying to find the base of a valley (the root) by always walking along the steepest downward slope.

sections.title: The Newton Iteration Formula
sections.content: Introduce the mathematical formula: x_{n+1} = x_n - f(x_n)/f'(x_n). Explain this as a feedback loop. Use a graphical animation where a point jumps closer to the root with every step, demonstrating rapid convergence.
sections.example: A robotic arm adjusting its position based on the sensor error slope until it perfectly grips a bolt.

sections.title: When Convergence Breaks: The Basin of Attraction
sections.content: Explain that Newton's method doesn't always go to the nearest root. Sometimes it enters a chaotic loop or jumps between roots. Define the 'Basin of Attraction': the set of initial guesses that lead to a specific root.
sections.example: Three magnets placed on a table; a metal ball dropped at different spots is pulled to different magnets.

sections.title: The Birth of the Newton Fractal
sections.content: Extend to the complex plane. If we color every starting point based on which root it converges to, the boundaries become infinitely complex. Show a zoom-in animation of the boundary regions to reveal the self-similar fractal patterns.
sections.example: A 'Digital Map' where the borders between different territories (roots) show intricate, repeating snowflake-like patterns regardless of how much you zoom in.

sections.title: Summary and Philosophical Takeaway
sections.content: Conclude that simple deterministic rules (Newton's formula) can generate extreme complexity (Fractals). Reiterate that mathematical beauty often emerges from the limits of iterative processes.
sections.example: A tiny acorn (the formula) growing into a complex, infinite-looking oak tree (the fractal).
